7916aaf2b75f

In this meeting, Jiajin shared some AI knowled

ge about Graph RAG and discussed its differences from traditional RAG. The

team then reviewed the progress of last week

99s action items, includ

ing the Confluence usage standard, the Q1 timeline, and the functional desi

gn of each system layer.

p local-id

3fa31b1c20ad

The team further clarified the major modules o

f the Q

A system, including the data processing pipeline, data persiste

nce layer, tool set, agent layer, and user layer. Mentors also provided fee

dback on the system architecture diagram, timeline planning, documentation

standard, and team collaboration approach.

hr local-id

b9827a17-3388-4b48-8491-37a115a72b5d

MeetingMinutesof2026

01-JulyMVPFeatu

reRefinement,ModuleDivisionofLabor,andSubsequentActionItems-DiscussionSumma

ry

Discussion Summary

p local-id

668c97569f7e

Jiajin shared the concept of Graph RAG and exp

lained that it is more suitable for questions involving entities, relations

hips, and multi-hop reasoning. The team discussed that Graph RAG may be hel

pful for relationship-based queries, but it may also introduce higher token

cost, slower retrieval, and maintenance difficulties when the graph needs

frequent updates.

p local-id

3cbaf2666100

Yixi introduced the current Confluence setup.

Four Confluence spaces have been prepared for different groups, and each sp

ace includes a usage guide. The team discussed the need to divide documents

into relatively stable documents and continuously updated documents, so th

at future synchronization between Confluence and the local knowledge base c

an be tested more clearly.

p local-id

48245e96c27a

The team discussed two possible collaboration

models. One option is to divide work by module, so each subgroup focuses on

a specific system layer. The other option is to let all members participat

e in multiple modules, so that everyone can understand the whole project be

tter. After discussion, the team tentatively agreed to first proceed by mod

ule-based division for efficiency, and later allow members with extra capac

ity to support other modules.

p local-id

23e067ad9702

Guangyuan presented the data processing pipeli

ne. This layer is responsible for parsing documents, extracting document st

ructures, building section trees, splitting content into chunks, preserving

title paths, and preparing structured JSON output. The team also discussed

the possibility of using mature document parsing APIs or tools in the futu

re if the basic parser is not sufficient.

p local-id

db913d50d564

Jiajin presented the embedding and storage par

t of the data processing pipeline. This part includes selecting and configu

ring an embedding model, implementing single-text and batch-text vectorizat

ion functions, and calling the data persistence layer to store vectors, ori

ginal text, document IDs, chunk indexes, and local JSON files.

p local-id

ddbf01aa25e1

Guangyuan also introduced the tool set layer.

The tool set acts as the bridge between the agent layer and the data persis

tence layer. The current Q1 focus is the search tool, which should support

semantic vector retrieval, BM25 retrieval, hybrid retrieval, top-k control,

score threshold filtering, and metadata filtering.

p local-id

88792d9614c4

Huifang and Suijie presented the agent layer.

The agent layer receives the user question, validates the input, generates

a trace ID, calls the retrieval tool, assembles the prompt, calls the LLM,

generates the answer, returns citations, and handles exceptional cases. The

Q1 agent will focus on a single-turn RAG agent rather than a complex multi

-agent or multi-turn system.

p local-id

2573cf1557c3

Jiaxing and Daijiang presented the user layer.

Jiaxing focused on the basic web page, chat interface, input box, message

display, loading state, and streaming display effect. Daijiang focused on t

he interface connection between the web layer and the agent layer, includin

g Agent API calling, response parsing, status mapping, streaming token hand

ling, error display, mock data, and mock API for independent frontend testi

ng.

p local-id

9b5e5c5282e3

Tao suggested that the system architecture dia

gram should be further optimized. The diagram should clearly show what each

layer needs to achieve for Checkpoint 1, while detailed implementation cho

ices such as specific vector databases or retrieval algorithms can be left

in separate documents.

p local-id

32037d505bb7

Loura suggested that, in addition to the Q1 ti

meline, the team should also prepare an overall project timeline slide. She

also reminded the MoM noter to attach the one-page slide and the Confluenc

e page standard to the meeting minutes.

p local-id

f8e8ec3b7b2f

Tao also suggested that project documents shou

ld be written in English as much as possible, since HSBC is an internationa

l company and most internal documents are usually written in English.

0f648955-c1fa-48e9-8180-a433b87d9cfc

at future synchronization between Confluence and the local knowledge base c
The team discussed two possible collaboration

Guangyuan presented the data processing pipeli

title paths, and preparing structured JSON output. The team also discussed
the possibility of using mature document parsing APIs or tools in the futu
re if the basic parser is not sufficient.
Jiajin presented the embedding and storage par
t of the data processing pipeline. This part includes selecting and configu
ring an embedding model, implementing single-text and batch-text vectorizat
ion functions, and calling the data persistence layer to store vectors, ori
ginal text, document IDs, chunk indexes, and local JSON files.
Guangyuan also introduced the tool set layer.
The tool set acts as the bridge between the agent layer and the data persis
tence layer. The current Q1 focus is the search tool, which should support
semantic vector retrieval, BM25 retrieval, hybrid retrieval, top-k control,
score threshold filtering, and metadata filtering.

The agent layer receives the user question, validates the input, generates

generates the answer, returns citations, and handles exceptional cases. The
Q1 agent will focus on a single-turn RAG agent rather than a complex multi
